profile.name: Chayne Wild
profile.title: Ph.D. Candidate in ASPECT
profile.lead: I am a Ph.D. Candidate in the Alliance for Social, Political, Ethical, and Cultural Thought (ASPECT) at Virginia Tech.

researchInterests.title: Carceral Studies & Decolonial Theory
researchInterests.description: Focused on the "carceral digital turn" and the evolution of prisoner resistance. My research utilizes the American Prison Writing Archive (APWA) to center the lived experiences and "shadow canons" of incarcerated intellectuals, challenging state-sanctioned narratives of technological control.

researchInterests.title: Critical Sociology & Social Thought
researchInterests.description: Investigating the intersection of racial capitalism, surveillance, and epistemic authority. I draw on Stuart Hall, Frantz Fanon, and Karl Marx to theorize how carceral technologies—from electronic monitoring to digital communication platforms—reproduce colonial hierarchies and how these systems are contested from within.

manuscripts.title: “Frantz Fanon’s Influence on Francesc Tosquelles and the Post-Colonial Legacy of Institutional Psychotherapy”
manuscripts.venueHtml: Target: Theory, Culture, and Society (6,000–8,000 words).
manuscripts.abstract: A qualitative article investigating the inverse relationship of influence between Fanon and Tosquelles. This research traces how Fanon's organic activist focus and concept of “sociogeny” fed back into the institutional psychotherapy movement.

courses.name: PSCI 2014: Introduction to Political Theory
bullets: Theories of Self, Care, and Technology (Spring 2023): Redesigned the curriculum around the goal of gnothi seauton ("Know Thyself") in the post-information age. Explored the intersections of neurobiology, phenomenology, and psychoanalysis to interrogate governmentality and the impact of AI and social media.

Human Nature, Ethics, and Resistance (Fall 2022): Facilitated a traditional survey of foundational thought (Machiavelli, Plato, Hobbes) updated with a focus on direct action and the ethics of violence (Graeber, Butler, Malm).

Digital Humanities & Applied Theory (Summer 2022 – Online Asynchronous): Adapted materials into a condensed digital format. Produced an original political theory podcast with guest speakers and mentored students through creative digital humanities final projects.

courses.name: PSCI 1014: Introduction to US Government and Politics
bullets: Designed an experiential curriculum focused on institutional organizations and direct action. Rigorous, discussion-heavy seminar style combined with engaging activities.
Mock-Trial Exercise: Conducted an immersive mock-trial to apply critical legal and political theory to procedural practice.
Guided student-led democratic campaigns on campus safety and rights, overseeing FOIA requests and media outreach.
